earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description is a wordlist or less only (Zvelebil 1997; Singh 1994; Hivale 1946; Russell & Hiralal 1916); no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Hivale, Shamrao. 1946. The Pardhans of the Upper Narbada Valley. Oxford University Press. (DLI scan, archive.org scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnography with song texts in translation; no language chapter. Only linguistic remark: a lower Pardhan sub-division 'speak more Marathi than Gondi' (Introduction, citing Hislop); refers readers to Trench, A Grammar of Gondi (1919) for Gondi words.

sources.citation: Russell, R. V. & Hira Lal. 1916. 'Pardhan', in The Tribes and Castes of the Central Provinces of India, vol. IV, pp. 352-358. London: Macmillan. (archive.org scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic article ('An inferior branch of the Gond tribe whose occupation is to act as the priests and minstrels of the Gonds'); no remarks on language, dialect or stress at all.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page Northern Gondi (nort2702, ISO gno).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Used only to fix the glottocode of the Gondi variety the Pardhan of Seoni/Balaghat/Mandla report speaking.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classified 'Unattested: Pardhan'; reference list contains only overview/ethnographic/socling items, no grammar, sketch, phonology or wordlist.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; calls Pardhan 'a dialect of Gondi spoken by the Pardhan people' and notes Glottolog lists it as unattested; cites only Ethnologue and the SIL 2008 survey.

sources.citation: Valte, Thangmualian; Eldose K. Mathai; Symon George. 2008. A sociolinguistic survey among the Pardhan community of central India. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-018, 4 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology. Fieldwork (Seoni, Balaghat, Mandla, Aug 2005) concluded: '(1) Pardhan does not appear to be a distinct language at this time and (2) Pardhan people speak dialects of Gondi as their mother tongue' (p. 4, sec. 7); 'the researchers were not able to locate any other published information that specifically refers to or describes Pardhan as a separate language' (p. 3, sec. 5).

sources.citation: Subrahmanyam, P. S. 1968. A Descriptive Grammar of Gondi (Adilabad). Annamalai University. Phonemics excerpt (10 pp.) as posted by The Rosetta Project.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Excerpt (phoneme inventory and allophones, sec. 1.1-1.2) contains no stress/accent statement; describes Adilabad (Southern) Gondi, not Pardhan; examined only as context.

sources.citation: Trench, C. G. Chenevix. 1919. Grammar of Gondi as spoken in the Betul District, Central Provinces, India. 2 vols. Madras: Government Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; only the abstract or a snippet was reachable when a reader tried
sources.note: Grammar of the Northern Gondi of the Satpura region where Hivale's Pardhans live (Hivale 1946 refers readers to it); would supply the Gondi-variety stress statement if one is wanted for the Pardhan area specifically.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages. (archive.org scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 3254.1 F; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 5.40; a Harvard library, call number Ud 0010
sources.note: No entry or mention of Pardhan/Pradhan as a Gondi variety (a full-text search for stress/accent full scanned text: no hits); the Gondi chapter is not variety-specific to Pardhans.
